3.0.0.en: 1 Then said the LORD unto me, “Go yet, love a woman beloved of her friend, and an adulteress, according to the love of the LORD toward the children of Israel, who look to other gods and love cakes of raisins.”

3.0.1.en: Since scholars refuse to accept what is recorded here as a second marriage different from the one recorded in the first chapter, why did he repeat the event of marrying an adulteress?

3.1.0.en: First: some scholars hold that his wife Gomer the daughter of Diblaim fled from the marital home and sold herself to corruption, so that she became a slave, but the prophet returned and bought her for himself as a wife [2].

3.1.1.en: Second: some hold that what is recorded in this chapter is the very same thing that is recorded in the first chapter, but whereas the first chapter gave the command to marry, here he relates what actually happened, presenting to us the experience the prophet himself went through.

3.1.2.en: Third: a few scholars hold that the first account was directed to the northern kingdom (Israel), whereas here the account is directed to the southern kingdom (Judah), despite his saying “the children of Israel,” for the first kingdom was divorced and carried captive, and the second remained for a century and was also divorced and carried captive afterward.

3.1.3.en: Fourth: some hold that what is recorded here is merely a repetition of what is recorded in the first chapter, as an affirmation of God’s love for His fallen bride, and giving her more than one opportunity to reflect on the love of her first husband for her.

3.1.4.en: In the first chapter the Lord said to Hosea, “Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms,” but here He says to him, “love a woman beloved of her friend and an adulteress.” So the command came to him not merely to marry her as God’s command, but to love her despite his knowing that she was beloved of a friend and that she was an adulteress. Thus God wanted Hosea to enter into the fellowship of the love that God has toward His people, despite what this people had done, turning to other, pagan gods and eagerly taking part in corrupting feasts, for He says to him, “according to the love of the LORD toward the children of Israel, who look to other gods and love cakes of raisins” [1].

3.2.0.en: “So I bought her to me for fifteen shekels of silver, and for a homer and a lethech of barley” [2].

3.2.1.en: If this woman, in the desires of her heart, sold herself to the account of evil and became a lowly slave, so that her price became fifteen shekels of silver, that is, less than the price of a female slave; she ran after her lovers and offered her life as a vow to them, and so became worthless, for she lost her dignity and her glory, and lost the image in which her God had created her, who in His love had set her up in His image and likeness.

3.2.2.en: In any case, since Hosea is a type of Jesus Christ the Savior, his purchase of the adulterous woman points to His salvation of us, for He bought us with His precious blood from the bondage under whose yoke we ourselves had taken ourselves captive.

3.2.3.en: The prophet Hosea says, “I bought her to me.” Our Lord Jesus Christ acquired for Himself a bride who dedicates all her energies to His account, and not to the account of the world or Satan.

3.2.4.en: As for the price that Hosea paid, it was very paltry: fifteen shekels of silver, that is, less than the price of a male slave (Ex 21:22), and a homer and a lethech of barley and not wheat (Ps 81:16); the world valued her at barley, the food of the poor or of animals, and she deserved no more than this in its eyes. But our Lord Jesus acquired us not with gold or silver, nor with wheat or barley, but with His precious blood, as the Apostle says: “Knowing that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers, but with the precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, the blood of Christ” (1 Pet 1:18-19).

3.3.0.en: 3 And I said unto her, “Thou shalt abide for me many days; thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt not be for another man: so will I also be for thee.” 4 For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod and teraphim.

3.4.0.en: If God in His love runs after adulterous humanity, redeeming her with His blood, it is only in order to sanctify her and so prepare her for the heavenly wedding. For He says, “And I said unto her, ‘Thou shalt abide many days; thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt not be for another man: so will I also be for thee’” [4]. The holy Son of God dedicated His work to the account of this wedding, saying, “so will I also be for thee,” and more clearly He says, “And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth” (Jn 17:19). The Holy One sanctified His life, that is, dedicated it to our salvation, so that we may be sanctified by Him, offering our lives to Him through sanctification by His blood by means of His Holy Spirit. And the wonder is that the soul’s spiritual marriage to God not only removes from her her uncleanness or spiritual adultery, but grants her “virginity.” As St. John Chrysostom says: [The Church is called a virgin, she who was formerly an adulteress. This is the miracle which the Bridegroom wrought: He took her as an adulteress and made her a virgin! What a wonderful and new thing! For through marriage we lose our virginity, but God through marriage restores her virginity to the Church… When you hear these things, do not understand them in a material way, but soar high in your thought. Do not understand them in a bodily way… for the Church which you live is spiritual, not material.]

3.4.1.en: The prophet continues his speech: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image (an altar, according to the Septuagint), and without an ephod and teraphim” [4]. This is a reference to the period of captivity, in which the people were deprived of the freedom to worship God and all its privileges, and of every outward appearance of theirs as a nation or a church. Perhaps God permitted it as a period of preparation for them to receive true worship after they had been deprived of it because of their wickedness. God in His love deprives man even of blessings for a time, so that we may receive them in a greater and more lasting way!

3.5.0.en: 5 Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the LORD their God, and David their king; and shall run in fear to the LORD and to his goodness in the latter days.

3.5.1.en: He concludes the discourse on the acceptance of the adulteress into married love with the return of the Jewish people to the knowledge of God. Origen holds that the period of deprivation spoken of above does not refer only to the period of captivity, but also to the Jews’ rejection of the Messiah; yet in the last days they will accept the faith and join as members in the body of Christ to enjoy salvation, for he says: “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the LORD their God, and David their king; and shall run in fear to the LORD and to his goodness in the latter days” [5]. At the end of the ages they will run in fear to the Lord, or flee to Him.

3.5.2.en: Why does he say, “run in fear to the Lord”? Perhaps because they realize what sin did to David their king, that is, the Lord Christ, who is “the root and the offspring of David” (Rev 22:16), and they run in fear to Him to work out their salvation with fear and trembling (Phil 2:12).

4.0.0.en: 1 Hear the word of the LORD, ye children of Israel: for the LORD hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no faithfulness, nor kindness, nor knowledge of God in the land. 2 Cursing, lying, killing, stealing, and committing adultery; they use violence, and blood toucheth blood. 3 Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field and the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away.

4.0.1.en: God directs the accusation to the children of Israel, calling them the earth, or the inhabitants of the earth, and declaring the substance of the charge, saying:

4.1.0.en: “Hear the word of the LORD, ye children of Israel: for the LORD hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no faithfulness, nor kindness, nor knowledge of God in the land. Cursing, lying, killing, stealing, and committing adultery; they use violence, and blood toucheth blood” [2].

4.1.1.en: Since the children of Israel became attached to the love of earthly things, they became earth, and the substance of the charge is this:

4.1.2.en: First: from the negative side He says: “there is no faithfulness (in the Septuagint “truth”), nor kindness, nor knowledge of God in the land.” Israel came under trial as earth that had lost its union with the heavenly Bridegroom, because it carries within it neither truth, nor mercy, nor the knowledge of God. Without this inseparable trinity in his life, man descends to the transient earthly nature.

4.1.3.en: He begins with faithfulness or truth, as the Lord Christ says in His farewell prayer, “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth” (Jn 17:17). They rejected the word of God and so rejected the truth, although it is not far from them: “The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach” (Rom 10:8). This truth must be joined to kindness or mercy, so that the word of God, or faith in it, is not merely memorized words or purely intellectual thought, but must touch our lives. And when the truth within us is turned into action, the “knowledge of God” increases in us and our insight is enlightened all the more. Thus truth interacts with action and knowledge, since they represent aspects intertwined together that belong to our life in Christ Jesus.

4.1.4.en: Second: since Israel lost this trinity of faith, action, and spiritual knowledge, it bore corruption: “Cursing, lying, killing, stealing; they use violence (they employ force), and blood toucheth blood.”

4.1.5.en: This list of sins declares at its beginning their breaking of the Ten Commandments (commandments 3, 9, 6, 8, 7), that is, the breaking of the covenant with God. As for his saying “they use violence,” it means the use of acts of violence contrary to the gentle Spirit of God. Perhaps it also means that they transgressed their bounds with God by violence, or that in their sins they transgress reason, conscience, or the Law not out of weakness or without will, but deliberately and violently. And by saying “blood toucheth blood,” he perhaps meant the blood of Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, who was stoned in the court of the house of the LORD at the command of King Joash (2 Chr 24:21), so that his innocent blood was mingled with the blood of the sacrifices which they offered in a crooked spirit.

4.2.0.en: Third: he concludes his accusation of the children of Israel by saying: “Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field and the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away” [3]. When Israel breaks God’s covenant it turns into a wilderness land that knows neither joy nor peace, but mourning and turmoil. There is no fruit in it, but famine and drought, and not even the wild animals, or the birds of heaven, or the fishes of the sea find food in it, but all languish. The fruit of breaking the covenant is a comprehensive ruin that touches the whole land with its animals, its birds, and its fishes.

4.2.1.en: He says, “the land shall mourn.” If the earth signifies the body for whose sake man commits evil to give it pleasure, then the fruit of this evil is the deprivation of this body of rest and joy, so that it remains mourning! This is the fruit of breaking the covenant with God, the Giver of peace, whereas union with Him gives man in his entirety true peace. As Fr. John of Kronstadt says: [When Christ dwells in the heart by faith, peace and joy dwell in it. For it is not without cause that God is said to be holy and to rest in His saints.] He also says: [I see with the eyes of my heart how I breathe in Christ in my heart with the mind, how He enters it and suddenly gives it peace and joy. Do not leave me to dwell alone without You, O Giver of life, my breath, my joy! For it is hard for me to be left without You.]

4.2.2.en: “And every one that dwelleth therein shall languish,” that is, man’s energies wither and his gifts are squandered, like the younger son who squandered his money in riotous living, so that he becomes like a dead man without worth, or a body without vitality. But the true believer praises truly, saying: “Thou visitest the earth, and makest it overflow; thou greatly enrichest it; the rivers of God are full of water… Thou blessest the fruits thereof. The pastures of the wilderness drop, and the little hills are girded with joy; the valleys are clothed with righteousness; they shout for joy, they also sing” (Ps 65:9, 13). It is as though he says to God: Even if I am dry earth, You tend me and make it overflow with goodness, sanctifying all Your gifts to me; You enrich it greatly, and fill my life with the waters of the Holy Spirit, who kindles all energies for the account of Your Kingdom; and You bless my inner produce, which is Your fruit in me, making my life fruitful and filled with joy and gladness, so that it speaks with praise and spiritual songs.

4.2.3.en: As for his saying: “with the beasts of the field and the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away,” in it there is a reference to the corruption of man’s life from every side: the land where the animals are, the air where the birds are, and the waters where the fishes are. The ruin has become so comprehensive that the wild animals, accustomed to the desolate wilderness, cannot live because of the severity of the drought, the birds of heaven find nothing to pick up, and even the fishes flee to other shores. Moreover, from another side, perhaps he wanted to reveal in his trial the gravity of sin, for it corrupts life, so that the ruin extends to the irrational creation of animals, birds, and fishes, as happened at the beginning of human life when the earth was cursed because of Adam and Eve and began to bring forth thorns and thistles. And from yet another side, perhaps the beasts of the field signify the bodily (animal) life, the fowls of heaven the thought, which it is fitting should soar in heavenly things, and the fishes of the sea the side of faith, as though man by leaving his heavenly Bridegroom shatters his life from all its sides, body, thought, and spirit, and loses all that he has.

4.3.0.en: 4 “Yet let no one judge, and let no one rebuke. For thy people are as they that strive with the priest. 5 Therefore shalt thou stumble in the day, and the prophet also shall stumble with thee in the night, and I will destroy thy mother. 6 My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children. 7 As they were increased, so they sinned against me: therefore will I change their glory into shame. 8 They eat up the sin of my people, and they lift up their souls to their iniquity. 9 And there shall be, like people, like priest: and I will punish them for their ways, and reward them their doings. 10 For they shall eat, and not have enough: they shall commit whoredom, and shall not increase: because they have left the service of the LORD.”

4.3.1.en: Having announced His trial of all the children of Israel and presented the substance of the charge, He called for the trial of the priests, together with the false prophets, as those first responsible for what this people had come to.

4.4.0.en: He says: “Yet let no one judge (other than him), and let no one rebuke. For thy people are as they that strive with the priest. Therefore shalt thou stumble in the day, and the prophet also shall stumble with thee in the night, and I will destroy thy mother” [5]. Perhaps he means here that every person is responsible for himself, and no one may justify the priest’s conduct merely because he is a priest, for since he stumbles by day, and with him the false prophets stumble by night through vain dreams, all share in the ruin of Samaria, the capital of Israel, their mother. It is as though the wicked priests had united with the false prophets in stumbling by day and by night, shattering the whole people.

4.4.1.en: Some hold that the address here is directed to the people, where God asks that the sincere reprovers be silent and withdraw from this work, because there is no one who listens to the voice of reproof, so that they have become so hardened that they reject all guidance even if a priest offers it. They strive with the priest who is frank with them, and even persecute him, as Joash king of Judah and his people did when they stoned Zechariah the son of Jehoiada in the court of the house of the LORD because he spoke the words of the LORD (2 Chr 24:21).

4.5.0.en: God directs His speech to the priests, declaring that they destroyed the people through lack of knowledge: “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me” [6]. We have already clarified in the introduction to the book what is meant by the knowledge of God in this book, and we saw the link between the knowledge of God and the godly life made holy in the Lord. The priests left the life of fellowship with God and busied themselves with their own interests, so they lost godly knowledge and became like those who are in the darkness of ignorance. He did not say, “because thou art ignorant,” but “because thou hast rejected knowledge”; as though He says to him: You are without excuse, for knowledge is available to you and the light is present, but you reject knowledge and do not accept the light, as it is said: “they have no delight in the knowledge of the ways of God” (Job 21:14). The secret of their rejection of knowledge is their abandoning of the word of God or the commandment: “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children” [6]. Thus He links the knowledge of God with the law of God, since the latter is its source. As Fr. John of Kronstadt says: [Holy Scripture is the center of God’s wisdom, His word, and His Spirit… In it He declares of Himself: “The words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life” (Jn 6:63). In Holy Scripture we see God face to face, and we see ourselves as we are, so that man knows himself through it, and walks always in the presence of God.]

4.5.1.en: And if we take the symbolic meaning, who is the priest who rejects the knowledge of God so that all the people perish, and forgets the law of God so that God forgets his children, if not the heart, which ought to have been the center of the Kingdom of God, yet is attached to the world and temporal things, and so loses its purity and does not see God, but becomes like one in spiritual blindness without living knowledge, forgetting the commandment or pretending to forget it. This heart that rejects knowledge through purity destroys all the people, that is, the whole body with its energies and capacities, and when it forgets the divine commandment the commandment bears no fruit in it, so that it is like one who has forgotten her children.

4.5.2.en: By this we understand what we have said before, that knowledge is not acquired through reading alone but through the godly life of devotion made holy in the Lord, through the inner priest, that is, the pure heart which intercedes for the whole body before God.

4.6.0.en: The Lord continues His rebuke of the priests, saying: “As they were increased, so they sinned against me: therefore will I change their glory into shame. They eat up the sin of my people, and they lift up their souls to their iniquity. And there shall be, like people, like priest: and I will punish them for their ways, and reward them their doings. For they shall eat, and not have enough: they shall commit whoredom, and shall not increase: because they have left the service of the LORD” [7-10]. They relied on the multitude of their number or the quantity of work and not on its quality, therefore “as they were increased, so they sinned against me”; instead of their inner sanctification and their true witness before the people of God, they became all the more sinners against God. They were occupied with pagan feasts and fell into abominations, therefore they were condemned together with the people without partiality.

4.6.1.en: “They eat up the sin of my people,” that is, they eat the sin offerings which the people present, so they are not concerned with the people’s repentance and their turning back from evil, but rejoice in the people’s offering of sacrifices for the sake of their own enjoyment of the sacrifices, for the more the people sinned, the more their portion increased through the abundance of sacrifices! They were concerned not with repentance but with filling their bellies with meat at the expense of the people’s sanctification. Therefore they eat and are not satisfied, and commit adultery by taking concubines, so the blessing is removed from them. It is a hideous picture unbecoming of a priest, therefore Fr. John of Kronstadt warns us, saying: [The priest is an angel, not a man, and it is fitting for him to cast every worldly matter far behind him. O Lord, may Your priests be clothed with righteousness (Ps 132:9). May they remember always the greatness of their calling, and not fall into the snares of the world and Satan, but be delivered from the cares of the world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of all other things that enter their hearts (Mk 4:19).]

4.7.0.en: 11 “Whoredom and wine and new wine take away the heart. 12 My people ask counsel at their stocks, and their staff declareth unto them: for the spirit of whoredoms hath caused them to err, and they have gone a whoring from under their God. 13 They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills, under oaks and poplars and elms, because the shadow thereof is good! Therefore your daughters shall commit whoredom, and your daughters-in-law shall commit adultery. 14 I will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery: for themselves are separated with whores, and they sacrifice with those who vow whoredom: and the people that doth not understand shall be overthrown. 15 Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah offend; and come not ye unto Gilgal, neither go ye up to Beth-aven, nor swear, The LORD liveth. 16 For Israel slideth back as a backsliding heifer: now the LORD will feed them as a lamb in a large place. 17 Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone. 18 When their carousing is ended, they commit whoredom upon whoredom. Her shields love, they love disgrace. 19 The wind hath bound her up in her wings, and they shall be ashamed because of their sacrifices.”

4.7.1.en: After announcing His trial of all the children of Israel, especially the religious leaders, He reveals the abominations into which all had fallen:

4.7.2.en: First: “Whoredom and wine and new wine take away the heart” [11]. Their turning from the worship of God to the worship of Baal was caused by bodily pleasures, and as St. Augustine says, behind every atheism there is a lust. For the lusts of the flesh, if left without restraint, corrupt the heart and kill in it every longing for God as the Bridegroom of the soul, so man resorts to fleeing from God, regarding Him as one who stifles his breath and shatters his personality.

4.7.3.en: Second: when man gives himself over to the enjoyment of bodily pleasures without restraint, he descends to improper and unacceptable conduct such as acts of sorcery, which were at that time linked with the worship of Baal. God says: “My people ask counsel at their stocks (perhaps the wooden statue of Baal), and their staff declareth unto them.” Instead of turning to the Lord their God and asking Him for counsel, they began to resort to the statue of Baal and acts of sorcery to determine their way for them and reveal the future to them. Everyone who leaves the word of God and resorts to the world and to men is like one who consults the wood and asks the staff.

4.8.0.en: Third: their rush into pagan worship; they offer sacrifices on the tops of the mountains and incense on the hills, and under the oaks, the poplars, and the elms, because the shadow thereof is good [13]. Israel encompassed mountains that ought to have been holy (Jer 31:23), to which those who desire salvation flee (Gen 19:17), upon which the heavenly Bridegroom comes leaping (Song 2:8), upon which the city of Jerusalem is built (Mt 5:14), so that it cannot be hid, to which the Lord Christ went up (Jn 6:3), and which drop down spiritual new wine unceasingly (Joel 3:18). These mighty mountains were turned to the account of the devil, and defiled altars were set up upon them.

4.8.1.en: And as Israel encompassed mighty mountains that were turned to the account of Baal, so it also encompassed smaller souls, which are the hills upon which the Lord Christ ought to have come leaping (Song 2:8); these too were corrupted and carried the smell of defiled incense.

4.8.2.en: What I say of the mountains and hills I repeat of the oaks, the poplars, and the elms, which, instead of glorifying God, became centers for the account of the kingdom of darkness.

4.8.3.en: In any case, the Jews chose the high places such as mountain summits and hilltops, not in order to rise by them in thought above earthly things, but to think that they had drawn near to heaven, and behold, they sank down to the abyss. And they chose the thick trees, thinking that they would help them in spiritual contemplation, instead of resorting to the shadow of the Cross and resting in the pierced side.

4.8.4.en: Finally He presents to us a hideous picture of the spread of adultery in their life, giving us the features of their defiled life, which are:

4.8.5.en: A. This sin was committed by unmarried daughters and by married daughters-in-law (the wives of the sons). It was as though the sin had become general, characterizing the female sex, so that the unmarried girl is not ashamed to commit it, nor is the married daughter-in-law ashamed of it.

4.9.0.en: B. It is as though God had despaired of them, for they committed the sin not out of weakness, nor in the midst of their striving, but were doing evil continually, without shame and by their own will; therefore God refuses to discipline them, and this is a punishment under which man falls, to be deprived of God’s fatherhood through God’s refraining from disciplining him, for He says: “I will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery” [14]. As Fr. Theodore says: [He is like a skilled physician who has used every means of treatment and there is no remedy left that can be used. God was overcome by their injustice and was compelled to cease His gentle disciplines, exposing them, saying: “So will I make my fury toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry” (Ezek 16:42).] And St. Jerome says: [Blessed is the man who is disciplined in this life, for God does not discipline twice for one thing [(Nah 1:9) Septuagint]. How great is the wrath of the Lord when He is not angry with us here, for by this He keeps us like an ox for the slaughter. In truth He says to Jerusalem that her sins are many and her evils great, therefore His jealousy departs from her and He is no more angry with her (Ezek 16:42). In other words He says: “When you were merely an adulteress I loved you and was jealous over you, but when you had many lovers I despised you, so I am not jealous and no more angry.” In the same sense, when a man loves his wife he is jealous over her, but when he hates her he does not say with God, “I will visit their transgression with the rod” (Ps 89:34), but says: “I will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom” (v. 14).]

4.9.1.en: C. What the daughters and women do is the natural fruit of the hideousness of what the men do, as He says: “for themselves are separated with whores, and they sacrifice with those who vow whoredom, and the people that doth not understand shall be overthrown” [14]. If the men and young men go to the altars of Baal scattered throughout all the land and are separated with harlots, offering sacrifices of evil with the priestesses who vow their lives to corruption for the account of Baal, then these men conduct themselves without understanding and are overthrown before defilement, or fall under sin; therefore God gave over their wives and their daughters to these lusts, for He says: “Therefore your daughters shall commit whoredom, and your daughters-in-law shall commit adultery” [13]. Thus God bitterly disciplines adulterers so that they may realize the hideousness of their conduct, as He formerly punished David by the defiling of his concubines (2 Sam 2:11).

4.10.0.en: D. He describes them in their commission of this evil as the backsliding heifer [16] that does not accept the yoke, and when it is put upon her she balks to resist and goes back instead of walking forward with it to fulfill the purpose of her owner. Thus this people rejected the yoke of God’s commandment, and wanted to run madly after their own desire and not according to the will of God, and they went backward instead of advancing forward.

4.10.1.en: They set out for the places where adultery and pagan worship had spread, such as Gilgal and Beth-aven (the house of vanity), and so became like the lamb that feeds in a large place to be prepared for slaughter: “they grow fat and kick” (Deut 32:15).

4.11.0.en: E. He says: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone” [17], and in the Septuagint: “Ephraim is joined (or a partner) to idols, he places stumbling blocks for himself in his way.” He bound himself by himself to the idols, and so became a partner to them, bearing their traits in himself. Since they are of stone, his heart became of stone, and since they are transient and vain, he gave himself over to destruction and vanity.

4.11.1.en: Ephraim was joined to the idols and so became as one bound to them and enslaved to them, unable to hear good counsel or to be freed from them. This is the nature of sin, as St. Anba Antony the Great says: [When the soul is ignorant of sin, sin is beloved to it, and even enslaves the soul that loves it and takes it captive.]

4.12.0.en: F. Finally He asks: what becomes of their carousing?! Or what will be the end of this bitter drink? “Her shields love, they love disgrace. The wind hath bound her up in her wings, and they shall be ashamed because of their sacrifices” [18-19]. They loved disgrace, that is, shameful gain and corruption, and received shame. And finally the raging wind carries them off into captivity, as on wings of evil, to bring them into the humiliation of bondage, and then they will be ashamed of their pagan sacrifices which could not save them.

4.12.1.en: If this people lived for a time in the spirit of the Gentiles, worshiping idols, then they will receive the desire of their heart when they are carried off as captives to where pagan worship is and to deprivation of Jerusalem and the temple of the Lord, and so taste the bitterness of the fruit of their work!
